summary.one_liner: A tutorial series that teaches how to build a minimal version of the Express.js web framework from scratch in Node.js.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a series of chapters that walk through re-implementing the express library step by step, with a running example at each stage. It says the code and variable names follow express itself so readers can later contribute to the real project. The chapters listed cover building the basic abstractions, routing, implementing the next function, extending the response object, adding send and json on the response, and error handling (marked as work in progress). The author states the minimal working library and its tutorial are done, while the series as a whole is still in progress with more chapters planned. The stated goal is to help readers understand how next and route ordering behave in express.
use_cases: study route ordering in web servers
follow a step-by-step Node.js framework tutorial
prepare to contribute to express source code
notable: Mirrors express's own code, variable names, and structure so the tutorial maps onto the real library
Chapter-by-chapter build-up with running examples at each step
Focuses on explaining next() and route order, which the author says people often find confusing
Listed under 'Build your own Web Server' in the codecrafters build-your-own-x collection
caveats: Work in progress: the error handling chapter is marked WIP and more chapters are planned
Not a production framework; it is a teaching reimplementation of a subset of express
README gives no install or run instructions
